query: What are the main types of concerns patients come in with in these visit notes?

per_column.name: concern_category
per_column.rationale: Directly answers the query by grouping visits into clinical concern types, giving a strong axis to aggregate and compare. Categories are well-grounded in the reason_for_visit text (e.g. knee pain->Musculoskeletal, MI follow-up->Cardiovascular). One borderline case: an annual physical with fatigue/BP/BMI was labeled 'Endocrine / Metabolic' when it is arguably preventive/general, a defensible but slightly overconfident reading, so groundedness is not perfect.

per_column.name: chief_complaint
per_column.rationale: Extracts the leading clause of reason_for_visit as a concise chief complaint. Values are faithful, near-verbatim extractions from the source. However for the query about MAIN TYPES of concerns it is largely a truncation of an existing column and highly high-cardinality (mostly singletons), so it offers limited grouping leverage beyond concern_category, though it still aids drill-down/verification.

judge.rationale: concern_category is a genuinely useful, well-grounded categorical axis that directly serves the 'main types of concerns' query. chief_complaint is faithfully extracted but mostly a restatement/truncation of reason_for_visit with high cardinality, limiting its analytical leverage for typing concerns. Both columns are soundly derivable from the source text with no invented facts; only minor overconfident categorisation (the physical-as-Endocrine case) slightly lowers groundedness.
